We’ve created GPT‑4, the latest milestone in OpenAI’s effort in scaling up deep learning.

GPT‑4 is a large multimodal model (accepting image and text inputs, emitting text outputs) that, while less capable than humans in many real-world scenarios, exhibits human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks.

For example, it passes a simulated bar exam with a score around the top 10% of test takers;

in contrast, GPT‑3.5’s score was around the bottom 10%.

*Updated October 2026*

GPT is one of the most searched model families in AI, and also one of the most confusingly named.

OpenAI has shipped dozens of versions, tiers and product surfaces since 2018: GPT-1 through GPT-6.1, Instant through Pro, and now Astra, Sol, Terra and Luna.

With so many names stacked on top of each other, how do you actually tell them apart?

This guide maps the whole lifecycle: the history, the current ChatGPT models, how the GPT-6 tiers compare on independent benchmarks, and how GPT compares to the alternatives.

The simplest way through it: GPT is the model family.

ChatGPT is the product.

| --- |

GPT-6 Luna is the low-cost tier.

In ChatGPT, paid plans chat with GPT-6 Sol, the Pro option uses Astra, and Free and Go users get GPT-6 Luna.
